- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is positive (especially >0.36) — model tends to overshoot.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (especially <0.28) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Forecast tends to lag true price declines — especially after sharp drops in sentiment or price, model doesn’t adjust quickly enough.
- After a price spike, model overcorrects downward, then re-overshoots upward — exhibit “overshoot-rebound” pattern.
- Mean reversion bias: model often forecasts prices to stay high after recent peaks, ignoring short-term volatility.
- Sentiment-driven bias: when sentiment is high, model forecasts higher than true; when sentiment is low, model forecasts lower than true — but with lag.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too optimistic in early days (first 5–7 days) and too pessimistic in late days (last 5–7 days) — model overweights recent sentiment but underweights long-term trend.
